title: Securities Trading Policy (STCS01)

tiers.name: Relevant Persons
tiers.description: All Directors of QBE, all Directors of the divisional statutory Boards of the QBE Group and all QBE Employees (employees, contractors, consultants and contingent workers). The insider trading, Closed Period, short-term dealing, secured financing and hedging prohibitions apply to every Relevant Person and their Closely Related Parties without differentiation.

tiers.name: Certain Relevant Persons (paragraph 6)
tiers.description: The persons listed in Column A of paragraph 6 who must obtain clearance for any dealing at any time, in or out of a Closed Period: Directors of QBE (including the Group CEO), the Chair, the Group General Counsel and Company Secretary, Group Executive Committee members, their direct reports, divisional statutory Board directors and chairs, and Executive Management Board members.

tiers.name: Directors of QBE
tiers.description: Directors of QBE including the Group CEO; cleared by the Chair of the QBE Board (the Chair by the Chair of the Audit Committee). Subject to initial, ongoing and final disclosure obligations to QBE under paragraph 11.

tiers.name: Members of the QBE Group Executive Committee
tiers.description: Group Executive Committee members including divisional CEOs, and the Group General Counsel and Company Secretary; cleared by the Group CEO.

tiers.name: Direct reports of members of the QBE Group Executive Committee
tiers.description: Direct reports of GEC members; cleared by their direct manager outside Closed Periods and by the Group CEO via the Group General Counsel and Company Secretary for a Closed Period waiver.

tiers.name: Directors of the divisional statutory Boards
tiers.description: Directors and chairs of divisional statutory Boards of the QBE Group and divisional General Counsels and Company Secretaries; cleared by the Chair of their divisional Board (chair by the divisional Board Audit Committee Chair).

tiers.name: Members of QBE Executive Management Board
tiers.description: Members of a divisional Executive Management Board (or equivalent), excluding the divisional CEO; cleared by their divisional CEO.

tiers.name: Any other Relevant Person
tiers.description: Relevant Persons not listed in paragraph 6. No clearance needed outside Closed Periods; a Closed Period or short-term dealing waiver requires the Group CEO via the Group General Counsel and Company Secretary.

tiers.name: Closely Related Parties
tiers.description: Section 9 Corporations Act meaning: spouse, child, spouse's child, dependants, other family members in a position of influence, and companies controlled by the Relevant Person. The Relevant Person must take reasonable steps to ensure compliance, obtain clearance on their behalf and report breaches.

definitions.hedging_definition: Hedging includes using securities to offset the risk of any adverse price movement in QBE securities or entering into transactions in financial products that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding QBE securities.

windows.start_anchor: 9.00am (Sydney time) on the date one week before QBE's annual balance date (preceding trading day if not a trading day)
windows.end_anchor: 5.00pm (Sydney time) on the day QBE's full results are released to ASX

windows.start_anchor: 9.00am (Sydney time) on the date one week before QBE's half-yearly balance date (preceding trading day if not a trading day)
windows.end_anchor: 5.00pm (Sydney time) on the day QBE's half-yearly results are released to ASX

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: QBE may determine and notify any other Closed Period from time to time (4.2(a)(iii)); the deciding officer and confidentiality are not specified.

rules.detail: The derivative definition expressly names options, forwards, swaps, caps and collars and any transaction limiting the economic risk of holding securities; derivatives (cash or physically settled, including third-party products) are QBE securities. Any risk-limiting derivative, including a put/call collar, is hedging and prohibited at all times. A non-risk-limiting derivative is a dealing subject to Closed Periods and, for paragraph 6 persons, prior clearance.
rules.evidence: derivative has the meaning given to that term in the Corporations Act and includes options, forward contracts, swaps, futures, warrants, caps, collars and any other transaction in financial products that operates to limit the economic risk associated with holding securities.

rules.detail: Absolute ban at all times on hedging any QBE securities, vested or unvested, plan or non-plan, for all Relevant Persons and Closely Related Parties. No waiver route: paragraph 5 waivers extend only to Closed Periods and short-term dealing.
rules.evidence: Hedging of QBE securities by a Relevant Person and their Closely Related Parties is prohibited at all times.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward is a forward contract limiting economic risk (hedging, banned) and any structure secured on QBE securities is a prohibited secured financial arrangement.
rules.evidence: entering into transactions in financial products that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding QBE securities.

rules.detail: Short selling is not named; a short position used to offset price risk would be hedging.
Stock lending is expressly a dealing, so it is barred in Closed Periods and needs prior written clearance from the Assessor for paragraph 6 persons; it is not otherwise prohibited.
rules.evidence: entering into margin lending, stock lending or other financing arrangements related to securities

rules.detail: A dealing subject to the insider trading and Closed Period rules only.
rules.evidence: entering into margin lending, stock lending or other financing arrangements related to securities

rules.detail: CFDs are not named but are cash-settled derivatives and so securities; a long CFD is a dealing requiring clearance and subject to the three-month rule, while a short CFD offsets price risk and is prohibited hedging.
rules.evidence: any derivatives of those securities, whether settled by cash or otherwise, including financial products created by third parties in relation to those securities.

rules.detail: Long CFDs are dealings subject to the Closed Period and short-term rules; short CFDs are prohibited hedging.
rules.evidence: any derivatives of those securities, whether settled by cash or otherwise, including financial products created by third parties in relation to those securities.

rules.detail: Entering a margin lending arrangement over QBE securities or transferring QBE securities into an existing margin loan account is not permitted for any Relevant Person or Closely Related Party.
rules.evidence: Dealing in QBE securities by Relevant Persons and their Closely Related Parties pursuant to a margin lending arrangement or any other secured financial arrangement is not permitted.

rules.detail: Pledging, collateralising or using QBE securities as security for any financing is expressly not permitted; granting a mortgage or other right over securities is also a dealing.
rules.evidence: pledging, collateralisation, or use of QBE securities as security for any other financing arrangement.

rules.detail: Blanket ban on any secured financial arrangement over QBE securities, for all tiers and security states, with no clearance or waiver route (paragraph 5 waivers cover only 4.2(a) and 4.2(b)).
rules.evidence: Dealing in QBE securities by Relevant Persons and their Closely Related Parties pursuant to a margin lending arrangement or any other secured financial arrangement is not permitted.

rules.detail: No purchase and sale of QBE securities within three months; waiver available from the Assessor for exceptional circumstances. Paragraph 7 exclusions (plan participation, DRP, SPP, rights issues, takeovers, no change of beneficial interest, ETF lookthrough, trading plans) are outside the rule.
rules.evidence: Relevant Persons and their Closely Related Parties must not deal in QBE securities on a short-term trading basis, being a period of three months between purchase and sale of any QBE securities.

clearance.approver: Chair of the QBE Board; for the Chair, the Chair of the QBE Audit Committee (or another Audit Committee member who is not the Chair). Group General Counsel and Company Secretary or Group Company Secretary to be notified.
clearance.post_trade_to: QBE (initial, ongoing and final disclosure of QBE and related body corporate securities under paragraph 11)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: unspecified (as required for ASX Listing Rule notifications)
clearance.evidence: In each circumstance, the duration of the clearance to deal in QBE securities will be five business days from the employees' receipt of the clearance. The Assessor may withdraw the clearance if new information comes to light or there is a change in circumstances.

clearance.tier: Members of the QBE Group Executive Committee
clearance.approver: QBE Group CEO (also for the Group General Counsel and Company Secretary); Group General Counsel and Company Secretary or Group Company Secretary to be notified
clearance.evidence: The Assessor may, in their discretion, grant or refuse a clearance, without giving any reasons.

clearance.tier: Direct reports of members of the QBE Group Executive Committee
clearance.approver: Their direct manager (Group CEO via the Group General Counsel and Company Secretary for a Closed Period waiver)
clearance.evidence: Where a clearance is refused, it is final and binding on the Relevant Person and the Relevant Person must keep all information relating to the clearance confidential.

clearance.tier: Directors of the divisional statutory Boards
clearance.approver: Chair of their divisional statutory Board (or another Board member in their absence); for a divisional Chair, the Chair of the divisional Board Audit Committee; divisional General Counsels and Company Secretaries and Closed Period waivers go to the Group CEO via the Group General Counsel and Company Secretary
clearance.evidence: If a Relevant Person or their Closely Related Parties listed in column A below intends to deal in QBE securities during any period (regardless of whether or not it is a Closed Period), the Relevant Person must seek clearance of the proposed dealing from the person(s) listed in column B below (Assessor)

clearance.tier: Members of QBE Executive Management Board
clearance.approver: Their divisional CEO (Group CEO via the Group General Counsel and Company Secretary for a Closed Period waiver)
clearance.evidence: Members of QBE Executive Management Board (or equivalent) (excluding the divisional CEO) - Their divisional CEO

clearance.approver: None outside a Closed Period; Group CEO via the Group General Counsel and Company Secretary for a Closed Period or short-term dealing waiver
clearance.evidence: Any other Relevant Person - The QBE Group CEO via the QBE Group General Counsel and Company Secretary

short_term.basis: period between purchase and sale of any QBE securities
carve_outs: Exceptional-circumstances waiver from the Assessor under paragraph 5

Paragraph 7 exclusions: employee equity plan participation, DRP/bonus share plan, SPP, rights issues, takeover acceptance, no change in beneficial interest, third-party managed vehicles holding QBE securities, pre-approved non-discretionary trading plans
short_term.evidence: Relevant Persons and their Closely Related Parties must not deal in QBE securities on a short-term trading basis, being a period of three months between purchase and sale of any QBE securities.

exceptions.approver: Assessor under paragraph 5 (Chair, Audit Committee Chair or Group CEO depending on the applicant)
exceptions.evidence: Exceptional circumstances for these purposes may include severe financial hardship, compulsion by court order or court enforceable undertaking, some other overriding legal or regulatory requirement to sell or transfer QBE securities, or any other circumstance that is deemed exceptional by the Assessor.

A waiver will only be granted if the Relevant Person's application is accompanied by sufficient evidence (in the opinion of the Assessor) that the requested dealing is the only reasonable course of action available in the circumstances.
participation in an employee equity incentive plan operated by QBE (e.g., applying for an allocation of QBE securities under an employee equity plan offer).
transactions undertaken solely to satisfy tax obligations may not require clearance where no discretion is exercised

acquisition of QBE securities through a QBE Board approved dividend reinvestment plan or bonus share plan ... acquisition of QBE securities through a share purchase plan available to all retail shareholders; acquisition or disposal of QBE securities through a rights issue or other pro rata entitlement offer
the disposal of QBE securities through the acceptance of a takeover offer

dealings that result in no effective change to the beneficial interest in the QBE securities (e.g., transfers of QBE securities already held into a superannuation fund or trust of which the Relevant Person or their Closely Related Parties is a beneficiary)

indirect and incidental trading that occurs as a consequence of a Relevant Person or their Closely Related Parties dealing in securities issued by a management investment scheme, listed investment company, exchange-traded fund or similar investment vehicle that is managed by a third party and that happens to hold QBE securities as part of its portfolio

trading under a pre-approved non-discretionary trading plan, where the Relevant Person and their Closely Related Parties did not enter into the plan or amend the plan during a Closed Period and the Relevant Person and their Closely Related Parties were not in possession of inside information at the time the Trading Plan was entered into

exemption_authority: Assessor (Chair of the Board, Chair of the Audit Committee or Group CEO per the paragraph 5 table) may waive the Closed Period (4.2(a)) and short-term dealing (4.2(b)) rules only, for exceptional circumstances on evidence the dealing is the only reasonable course; waiver lasts 5 business days and may be withdrawn. No authority to waive the hedging or secured financing bans. QBE Board approves the Policy.
jurisdiction_overlays: Relevant Persons outside Australia must also comply with applicable foreign insider trading, market abuse or securities laws (4.1(c))

bespoke_clauses.clause: derivative ... includes options, forward contracts, swaps, futures, warrants, caps, collars and any other transaction in financial products that operates to limit the economic risk associated with holding securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar is expressly a derivative and a risk-limiting transaction, so it is caught by the absolute hedging ban with no room for characterisation arguments.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Hedging of QBE securities by a Relevant Person and their Closely Related Parties is prohibited at all times.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The put and call legs are prohibited for all tiers over vested and unvested shares alike, and the paragraph 5 waiver power does not extend to hedging.

bespoke_clauses.clause: pledging, collateralisation, or use of QBE securities as security for any other financing arrangement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg secured on the collared shares is expressly not permitted regardless of whether the facility has margin-call mechanics.

bespoke_clauses.clause: entering into margin lending, stock lending or other financing arrangements related to securities; ... granting a mortgage or other right over securities to another party; and transferring legal ownership of securities
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even an unsecured financing referenced to QBE shares, or a transfer to a custodian or bank nominee, is a dealing subject to Closed Periods and clearance.

bespoke_clauses.topic: no waiver for hedging or financing
bespoke_clauses.clause: the Relevant Person may apply to the person(s) listed in the table below (Assessor) for a waiver from compliance with the provisions of that paragraph [4.2(a) or 4.2(b)].
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Exceptional-circumstances waivers cannot unlock a collar or secured loan; only Closed Period and short-term dealing relief is available.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where this Policy requires a Relevant Person to do something (e.g., obtaining clearance in accordance with paragraphs 5 or 6), that person must also do so for their Closely Related Parties.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Structuring the collar through a spouse, controlled company or family trust does not escape the hedging and secured financing bans.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any person who is proven to have breached this Policy could face disciplinary action (including forfeiture of QBE securities and/or suspension or termination of employment).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Forfeiture of QBE securities is a stated sanction, so collateral pledged in breach of the Policy is at risk.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Transactions effected through employee share plan administrators or platforms are considered dealings in securities for the purposes of this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Delivering vested plan shares to a bank via the plan administrator is itself a dealing requiring clearance.

summary: A funded collar is not possible under this policy for any director, executive or employee. Hedging of QBE securities, defined to include any transaction in financial products that limits the economic risk of holding them, is prohibited at all times for all Relevant Persons and their Closely Related Parties, and 'collars' are expressly named in the derivative definition, so the put and call legs are banned over vested and unvested shares alike. The loan leg is independently prohibited: paragraph 4.2(c) bars margin lending, transfers into margin accounts and any pledging, collateralisation or use of QBE securities as security for any financing arrangement, and granting a mortgage or other right over securities is a dealing. The paragraph 5 waiver power extends only to Closed Periods and the three-month short-term dealing rule, not to hedging or secured financing, and there is no other exemption authority. Paragraph 6 persons (directors, GEC members and their direct reports, divisional board directors and EMB members) need written clearance, valid for 5 business days, for any other dealing at any time.
